name: Dactinomycin
source_cmax: Veal et al. 2005, Clin Cancer Res (Newcastle ePrints 69998)
notes: paediatric data; adult PK largely unreported
how_it_works: Dactinomycin (actinomycin D) intercalates between guanine-cytosine base pairs in DNA, blocking the movement of RNA polymerase and thereby inhibiting transcription and RNA synthesis.

name: Vinblastine sulfate
cmax_conditions: NO reliable peak found: ~5 ng/mL 10 h after 3 mg/m2 bolus; 1-8 ng/mL during continuous infusion
source_cmax: Links et al. 1999 Cancer Invest; Weill Cornell phase I-II infusion study
notes: left blank deliberately - peak after bolus not found in a reliable source
how_it_works: Binds to beta-tubulin at the vinca domain, inhibiting microtubule polymerization and arresting cells in metaphase.

name: Tretinoin
cmax_conditions: single dose, mean (SD 266); falls to ~138 ng/mL with continued dosing
primary_target: Retinoic acid receptors (RAR-alpha, RAR-beta, RAR-gamma) and PML-RAR-alpha fusion protein
how_it_works: All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) binds to nuclear retinoic acid receptors and degrades the oncogenic PML-RAR-alpha fusion protein, inducing terminal differentiation and apoptosis of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) blasts.

name: Paclitaxel
cmax_conditions: 175 mg/m2 over 3 h, label PK table (n=5)
source_cmax: Paclitaxel label PK table (Pfizer / Gland Pharma SPL)
notes: label gives binding as 89-98%; midpoint used
how_it_works: Binds to beta-tubulin and stabilizes microtubules against depolymerization, thereby arresting cell division in mitosis.

name: Tamoxifen citrate
cmax_conditions: average steady-state concentration after 3 months (range 71-183); long half-life so peak is close
notes: active metabolite N-desmethyl tamoxifen at ~353 ng/mL not counted; binding not captured
how_it_works: Tamoxifen citrate is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) that competitively inhibits estrogen binding to its receptor in breast tissue.

name: Valrubicin
route: INTRAVESICAL ONLY - not for IV use
cmax_conditions: plasma 0-10 ng/mL after intravesical dosing (intact bladder)
notes: cannot be given systemically: will never reach a lung tumour
how_it_works: Valrubicin is a semisynthetic anthracycline derivative that penetrates into cells and inhibits the incorporation of nucleosides into nucleic acids, arresting the cell cycle in G2 phase by interfering with DNA topoisomerase II.

name: Mitoxantrone
cmax_conditions: APPROXIMATE: upper end of the plasma range (26-455 ng/mL) observed in patients per label binding data
notes: no labelled Cmax at standard dose; treat as approximate
how_it_works: Mitoxantrone is an anthracenedione antineoplastic agent that intercalates into DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II, causing DNA strand breaks and disrupting DNA replication and RNA transcription.

name: Docetaxel
source_dose: Docetaxel label: 75 mg/m2 single agent after platinum failure
how_it_works: Docetaxel is a taxane that binds to beta-tubulin, stabilizing microtubules and preventing depolymerization, which causes mitotic arrest and apoptosis.

name: Estramustine disodium phosphate
cmax_conditions: the tested compound (estramustine phosphate) is NOT detectable in plasma after oral dosing; only metabolites
notes: blood contains estramustine/estromustine, not the phosphate tested in vitro
how_it_works: Estramustine phosphate is a conjugate of estradiol and normustine that primarily exerts its antineoplastic effect in prostate cancer by binding to tubulin and microtubule-associated proteins to inhibit microtubule assembly and mitosis, alongside supplementary antigonadotropic activity.

name: Gefitinib
cmax_conditions: steady state, median (range 168-781), 35 EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients
source_dose: Gefitinib label (DailyMed / TGA PI): 250 mg daily
how_it_works: Gefitinib is a selective reversible inhibitor of the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain that blocks downstream pro-survival and proliferative signaling in cancer cells.

name: Lapatinib
how_it_works: Lapatinib is a reversible dual tyrosine kinase inhibitor that binds to the intracellular ATP-binding site of EGFR and HER2, blocking downstream signaling pathways involved in tumor cell proliferation and survival, primarily used in HER2-positive breast cancer.

name: Vismodegib
cmax_conditions: steady state, normal organ function, n=9
notes: unbound drug <1% of total (Graham et al. 2011)
how_it_works: Vismodegib inhibits the Hedgehog signaling pathway by binding to and inhibiting the transmembrane protein Smoothened (SMO), and is primarily used to treat basal cell carcinoma.

name: Cabazitaxel
how_it_works: Cabazitaxel is a semi-synthetic taxane that binds to tubulin to promote microtubule assembly and inhibit disassembly, resulting in mitotic arrest and apoptosis primarily used in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
